cycles.name: Foundation Forge
focuses: Groove the hip-dominant glute and posterior-shoulder patterns and build a posture base.
Establish a recovery rhythm and a strong mind-muscle connection in the delts and glutes.

paragraphs: This first block isn't about chasing big numbers — it's about building the platform everything else stands on. Your job right now is to own the hip-hinge and shoulder patterns, wake up the glutes and rear delts that drive both your shape and your posture, and get your recovery working for you.

Mentally, chase the feeling, not the load: every rep at the prescribed tempo, every squeeze felt exactly where it should be. By the end of five weeks you'll move cleaner, stand taller, feel your delts and glutes switch on the way they should — and you'll have laid the foundation for the visible change that starts in Cycle 2.
outcomes: Cleaner, more controlled hip-hinge and pressing patterns
Glutes and rear delts that switch on when they should — real mind-muscle connection
Better posture — shoulders sitting back, ribs and pelvis stacked
A recovery rhythm that works for you: steadier sleep quality and protected rest days
Confident tempo and RPE control on every main lift
A foundation set for the visible change that starts in Cycle 2

cycles.name: Growth Engine
focuses: Drive shoulder and glute hypertrophy with added volume and reps taken closer to failure.
Progressively load the supported primaries — press, hip thrust, hack squat.

paragraphs: Cycle 1 was about learning the patterns. This one is about making them show. Your shoulders and glutes get genuinely loaded now — more sets, taken closer to failure, on the lifts you've already proven you can drive.

The big change is shape. Shoulders now get two full days built entirely around them — Day 1 and Day 3 — instead of being squeezed in as an afterthought. They were the thing you asked for and the thing your logs said was most under-trained, so they're no longer stuck on the days that are easiest to skip.

Week one sits close to where Cycle 1 finished — you've had time away and we're re-entering, not restarting. From week two the volume climbs. Hit the RPE on the card, log every set the same way, and this is the block where the mirror starts agreeing with the work.
outcomes: Rounder, wider-looking delts — the shape you came here for
A heavier hip thrust, and a hinge you can finally load without grinding
Two full days built entirely around your shoulders now, not squeezed in
A back and rear delts strong enough to hold your posture without thinking about it
Core work you can actually feel, done where it belongs — at the end
A clean, readable log that shows exactly how much stronger you got

cycles.name: Metabolic Shift
focuses: Strip body fat while preserving the muscle already built to sharpen overall shape.
Hold training intensity in a deficit with strategic low-impact conditioning and steps.

paragraphs: Two cycles in, you have built something real. Now we make it show.

This block goes after body fat. The training stays hard on purpose, because the muscle you spent five weeks building is exactly what we are protecting. What changes is everything around it. Three days instead of four, two pairs of exercises run back to back to keep the pace up, and a walk to finish Day 3.
One thing is different this time. The scale is the scoreboard, and right now I cannot see it. Weigh in, log your real steps, and I can adjust this in week two instead of guessing until week five.
outcomes: A real weight line, not one reading
Steps you actually track, every day
Same strength at the end as the start
Three days that fit your week

cycles.name: Strength Engine
focuses: Intensify load on the primary lifts to raise the strength ceiling that future growth sits on.
Reinforce posture and bracing under heavier loads.

paragraphs: Cycle 4 is where we stop holding back. Once the fat is off, we go after the numbers. Heavier work on the lifts you already own, fewer reps, longer rests, and a proper strength ceiling to push against.
Everything you protect in this block is what you get to load in the next one.

cycles.name: Sculpt & Define
focuses: A specialised shoulder-cap and glute-shaping block to maximise the target aesthetic.
Lock in balanced 3-D delt development and the corrected posture.

days.completionMessage: That is your shoulder and upper back work done for the week. This is the session that changes how you stand, not just how you look.

good: Spin light and just raise your temperature
Feel your breathing settle into a rhythm
bad: Don't turn this into the workout

good: Slide your chin straight back over your collarbone
Feel the muscles at the front of your neck switch on
bad: Don't tip your head down, it slides back not forward

good: Open your top arm across and follow it with your eyes
Feel the mid-back rotate open
bad: Don't let your knees roll apart

good: Pull the band apart toward the walls either side of you
Feel it working between your shoulder blades
bad: Don't let your traps shrug up toward your ears

good: Slide your forearms up the wall and stay in contact
Feel the shoulder blades travel up and around
bad: Don't arch your lower back to get higher

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.note: You finished last cycle at 5 plates and held it there for four sessions straight. New gym means that number means nothing on a different machine, so find it again from your first set and log the actual kilos if the machine shows them.

good: Drive the handles straight up over your ears
Feel the front and side of the shoulder take it
bad: Don't arch your lower back to finish the rep

good: Pull the bar down to your collarbone
Feel your lats working, not your arms
bad: Don't lean back to drag it down

exercises.name: Cable Row
exercises.note: Sit tall and let your shoulder blades move. This one is here for your posture as much as your back, so the squeeze at the end matters more than the weight.

good: Pull the handle to your belly button and hold a beat
Feel your shoulder blades squeeze together
bad: Don't round your back at the start of the pull

exercises.name: Cable Face Pull
exercises.note: Set the cable at head height. This is the best exercise you have for pulling your shoulders back where they belong, so I would rather you did it well and light than heavy and sloppy.

good: Pull the rope to your forehead and split your hands apart
Feel the back of the shoulder and your mid-back
bad: Don't let it turn into a row into your chest

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.note: This is back because you love it. Last time we moved you off the cable because even the lightest pin was too heavy for fifteen controlled reps, so check that first at the new gym and use the band version if it is still too much. Keep it at 9, not 10.

good: Lead with your elbow, out toward the wall
Keep the burn on the side of the shoulder
bad: Don't swing your body to start the rep

exercises.name: Machine Lateral Raise
exercises.note: New one for you, and the reason it is here is that a machine starts lighter than the cable does. That was the exact problem with the cable version last cycle. If your new gym has no lateral raise machine, use the band version instead.

good: Push your elbows out into the pads and up to shoulder height
Keep the burn on the side of the shoulder
bad: Don't let the weight drop back down on its own

good: Bring your elbows down toward your knees
Feel the abs shorten from rib to hip
bad: Don't pull with your arms

days.completionMessage: That was the heaviest session of your week and you finished it. Eat well tonight and keep tomorrow easy.

good: Spin light and just raise your temperature
Feel your breathing settle into a rhythm
bad: Don't turn this into the workout

good: Push the floor away through your heels
Squeeze the glutes hard at the top
bad: Don't arch your back to get higher

good: Step wide and stay low the whole way
Feel the outside of the hip burning
bad: Don't let your knees cave inward

good: Push your hips back toward the wall behind you
Feel the hamstrings lengthen
bad: Don't round your back

good: Rotate both knees down to the floor on one side, then the other
Feel the hips open up
bad: Don't let your chest collapse forward

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.note: Your log shows 40 kg for 8 at a hard 9, held for two sessions. Start there, not above it. This is one of the lifts on your stop rule card, so tell me if anything builds low in the hip or belly through a set.

good: Drive the floor away and finish level at the top
Hold the squeeze at the top before you drop
bad: Don't let your ribs flare at lockout

exercises.name: Machine Hack Squat
exercises.note: This is the machine most likely to be missing at the new gym. If it is not there, use a Smith machine squat, and a goblet squat if there is no Smith either.

good: Push the platform away from you
Feel the front of the thigh through the whole rep
bad: Don't bounce out of the bottom

exercises.name: Cable Pull Through
exercises.note: This replaces the back extension you hated. Same job for the hips, nothing loading your spine. Push your hips back and let your arms just hold the rope, do not pull with them.

good: Throw your hips forward, not your arms
Feel the hamstrings load then the glutes finish it
bad: Don't squat it, keep the knees soft

exercises.name: Machine Lying Leg Curl
exercises.note: You swapped to this machine every single session last cycle instead of the ball, so I have written it in properly. Four sets here and three on the seated version, because two different angles beat six sets of the same thing.

good: Curl your heels toward your backside
Feel the hamstring shorten under the load
bad: Don't let your hips lift off the pad

exercises.name: Machine Seated Leg Curl
exercises.note: New one for you. It looks like the lying curl but your hips are bent, which hits a different part of the hamstring. Start light, it will feel harder than the lying version at the same weight.

good: Curl your heels down and under the seat
Feel the hamstring work from a different angle than the lying machine
bad: Don't let your hips slide forward out of the seat

exercises.name: Cable Hip Abduction
exercises.note: You told me you love this one so it stays. The change is the 2 second squeeze at the top, not more reps or sets. That hold is the whole progression, so actually hold it.

good: Drive the leg out and away from you
Feel the side of the glute hold the top
bad: Don't lean away to get more range

good: Reach your hands up toward your toes
Feel the abs fold you in half
bad: Don't let your lower back arch off the floor as you start each rep

days.completionMessage: Three for three, and you finished on the treadmill instead of skipping it. That walk is doing more for this cycle than you think.

Feel your breathing settle into a rhythm
bad: Don't turn this into the workout

good: Push the floor away through your heels
Squeeze at the top of every rep
bad: Don't arch your back to get higher

good: Open your top arm across and follow it with your eyes
Feel the mid-back rotate open
bad: Don't let your knees roll apart

good: Rotate both knees down to the floor on one side, then the other
Feel the hips open up

Feel the spine decompress

exercises.name: Machine Leg Press
exercises.note: This one is first in the session on purpose, not at the end, because it matters too much to be the thing you drop when time runs out. It was also the one machine where your weight climbed every single session last cycle.

good: Push the platform away through your whole foot
Feel the thighs and glutes share the load
bad: Don't let your lower back round off the seat at the bottom

exercises.name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
exercises.note: New movement. Start lighter than you think and let the first set tell you. Step back rather than forward, it is easier on the knee. If the gym is busy, the split squat you did last cycle works instead.

good: Step back and sink straight down
Feel the front glute and thigh take the weight
bad: Don't let the front knee cave inward as you stand up

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.note: You finished last cycle at 20 kg in each hand. Start there. Slow on the way down, that is where this one does its work.

good: Push your hips back and slide the dumbbells down your thighs
Feel the stretch down the back of your legs
bad: Don't round your back to reach lower

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
exercises.note: Chest stays on the pad the whole set. That is what stops your lower back helping and keeps the work in your upper back, which is the whole point of it being here.

good: Row the dumbbells up to your hips
Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top
bad: Don't lift your chest off the pad

exercises.name: Prone Y-T-W
exercises.note: This is the one that fixes rounded shoulders. Go very light or with no weight at all. If you feel it in your neck or your traps you are using the wrong muscles, so drop the weight and slow down. Lie face down on any incline bench, no machine needed.

good: Lift your arms off the bench and make the letter shapes
Feel the muscles low between your shoulder blades
bad: Don't shrug, the effort stays below your neck

exercises.name: Machine Chest Press
exercises.note: Light on purpose. You are working on pulling your shoulders back this cycle, so pressing is here to keep you balanced, not to be a focus. Keep the shoulder blades pinned back on the pad.

good: Press the handles away from your chest
Feel the chest doing it, not the shoulders
bad: Don't let your shoulders roll forward

exercises.name: Incline Treadmill Walk
exercises.note: Put the incline up until it feels like a hill and keep the speed at a walk. You should be able to hold a conversation the whole ten minutes. If Day 3 runs long, drop the core before you drop this.

good: Raise the incline until it feels like a hill and keep the speed a walk
You should be able to hold a conversation the whole way
bad: Don't hold the handrails, it takes the work out of it

cards.title: Twenty Out Of Twenty
cards.body:
Last cycle you trained 20 sessions out of 20. The cycle before that it was 9 out of 20.

And it was not just the easy days. You did all four days, five times each. The back half of your week used to never happen, and this time it happened every single week. You also finished about 96% of every set I wrote.

Read that again, because it is the hardest part of this whole thing and most people never get there. Everything in this cycle is built on the fact that you actually show up.

cards.title: When To Stop A Set
cards.body:
Nothing in your program is restricted and your bloods were reassuring. But you are the one in the room, so here is the line.

Normal and fine: muscles burning, feeling tired, being stiff the next day. Train through all of it.

Not fine: sharp pain, anything that radiates, numbness or tingling, or pain low in the abdomen or hip that builds through a set instead of staying flat.

  • Mild and fading, finish the set and tell me after.
  • Building, or changing how you move, stop that exercise and use the swap on the card, then message me.
  • Sharp, radiating, numb or just unfamiliar, stop the session and message me before the next one.

This matters most on the Barbell Hip Thrust, the Cable Pull Through, the Cable Hip Abduction and the V-Up. I would always rather hear about it early than find out a month later.

cards.title: One Reading Is A Dot
cards.body:
You logged your weight once. One reading is a dot. I need a line.

Weigh yourself in the morning, before eating, after the toilet, the same way every time. It does not have to be daily. Three or four times a week is plenty.

The app draws a 7 day average through your readings, and that line is the only number worth looking at. Your weight swings a kilo on water alone, so a single morning will lie to you. The average will not.

Nobody else sees this. It is not on the board, not on the wall, not shared with anyone. It is between you and me.

cards.title: I Cannot See Your Steps
cards.body:
Here is the honest situation. I do not know how much you walk.

On most days the step counter in the app has been tapped once, which puts 500 in. That is the smallest amount the app adds, not a measure of your day. So either you are walking very little, or you are walking and not logging it.

Your phone already counts your steps. At the end of the day, open it and put the real number in. That is the whole job.

I am asking because on a fat loss block, walking does more of the work than the gym does. Once I can see a real number for a week, we set a target you can actually climb. Until then I am guessing, and I would rather not guess with your time.

cards.title: Protein First, Every Meal
cards.body:
You already log 3 protein meals a day in the habit tracker, and through August you were hitting it. In the last week it slipped to one. That is the habit to protect in this block.

When you eat less, protein is what tells your body to keep muscle instead of burning it. It also keeps you full, which makes eating less a lot easier to live with.

Build each meal around the protein first, then add the rest. Meat, chicken, fish, eggs, dairy, whatever you actually like. I am not giving you numbers to count. Three meals, protein in each, logged. That is enough for this cycle.

Your sugar free habit was your own idea and it is a good one. Keep it.

cards.title: Pull More Than You Push
cards.body:
You told me you want a flat back. Right now your shoulders sit rounded forward and your head sits in front of them, and that is what this cycle is quietly working on underneath the fat loss.

Rounded shoulders do not get fixed by stretching your chest for two minutes. They get fixed by making the muscles between your shoulder blades strong enough to hold you up without you thinking about it. That is why you have four pulling exercises this cycle against one chest press.

Three of them are doing the real work. The Cable Face Pull and the Cable Row on Day 1, and the Prone Y-T-W on Day 3. None of them are heavy and none of them are supposed to be. If you feel any of them in your neck or the top of your traps, the weight is too high. Drop it, slow down, and find the muscles lower down between your shoulder blades.

Your Day 1 warm up is part of this too, not a formality. The Chin Tuck is for your head position and the Open Book is for your mid back. Do those two properly and they will do more for how you stand than anything else in the program.

cards.title: Week One, Go Lighter
cards.body:
There are seven movements in here you have never done before. In week one, run all of them at RPE 7, not the number written on the card.

The new ones are the Cable Row, Machine Lateral Raise, Cable Face Pull, Prone Y-T-W, Cable Pull Through, Machine Seated Leg Curl and the Dumbbell Reverse Lunge. The V-Up is new too.

Week one is for finding the right weight and learning how each one feels, not for proving anything. Pick something you are sure you can control, do all the reps, and see what the last set felt like. From week two, go to the number on the card.

Everything you already know how to do stays at the number on the card from day one.

cards.title: Your Period Week
cards.body:
This is a tool, not a rule. Use it on the days you need it and ignore it when you do not.

If a session lands on a bad day:

  • Barbell Hip Thrust and Machine Hack Squat, drop to 2 sets at a lighter weight. Move the pattern, do not chase the load.
  • Skip the ab work. The Cable Crunch on Day 1 and the V-Up on Day 2 are the first things to go, not the last.
  • Take 1 off every RPE on the card, but never go below 6.
  • Keep the walk on Day 3 if you can. Easy movement usually helps.

A short session still counts. Warm up plus the first two exercises is a real session. Log it and go home.

cards.title: Week Five Backs Off
cards.body:
This cycle runs five weeks, and week five is not another hard week. It is built in on purpose so you finish fresh instead of crawling to the end.

In week five only:

  • Cut about a third of the sets on every exercise.
  • Take 1 off every RPE, but never go below 6.
  • Keep the same weight. Less work, not lighter work.

This matters more than usual this time. You are eating less and your lifts are already sitting at a hard effort, so week five is what stops that turning into a wall.

cards.title: Your New Gym
cards.body:
You are moving gyms, so some machines will be different or missing. Do not skip the slot, swap it. Here is what to use.

  • Machine Shoulder Press, use the Smith machine shoulder press.
  • Machine Hack Squat, use a Smith machine squat, or a goblet squat if there is no Smith.
  • Machine Leg Press, use a goblet squat.
  • Lat Pulldown, use the assisted pull-up machine.
  • Cable Row, use a chest supported machine row.
  • Cable Face Pull, use a rear delt machine, or a band pulled apart at head height.
  • Prone Y-T-W, lie face down on any incline bench. You need no machine at all for this one.
  • Cable Lateral Raise, use the band version you did last cycle.
  • Machine Lateral Raise, use the band version too, or dumbbells if you prefer.
  • Cable Pull Through, use a dumbbell Romanian deadlift.
  • Machine Chest Press, use a dumbbell bench press.
  • Barbell Hip Thrust, use the hip thrust machine if they have one.
  • Incline Treadmill Walk, use the stair climber.

One thing I do not want back in your program is the 45 degree back extension. You told me five times you hate it, so it is gone for good. The Cable Pull Through does the same job.

If something is missing and it is not on this list, message me instead of guessing.

cards.title: Clean Slate On Your Log
cards.body:
New gym means every weight has to be found again anyway, so this is the perfect moment to fix one thing.

Right now, three of your main lifts tell me nothing. The Machine Shoulder Press, the Machine Hack Squat and the Machine Leg Press are logged as plate counts and pin numbers. A 5 on your old machine means nothing on a new one, and it means nothing to me either.

From your first session at the new gym, log the actual kilos and the reps you did. If the machine only shows numbers and no kilos, write the number and the reps and tell me which machine it is.

This is not admin. It is the difference between me adjusting your program from real numbers and me guessing from a stack of fives.
